project_inclusion.note: High-value Edwards Plateau species; locally relevant even if encountered less often.

morphology_keys.habit: Twining vine from a persistent rootstock.
morphology_keys.leaves: Broadly ovate to reniform, usually 3–5(–7)-lobed, cordate at base, hairy.
morphology_keys.sepals: Long lanceolate to lance-ovate sepals, about 18–30 mm, usually hairy.
morphology_keys.corolla: Large blue to violet funnel-shaped flower, about 55–90 mm long.
morphology_keys.key: Large blue-violet flower + palmately lobed hairy leaves + very long lanceolate sepals.

field_diagnostics.single_best_trait: The extreme flower/sepal scale is the giveaway: a 55–90 mm blue-violet corolla with 18–30 mm hairy sepals on a perennial vine.
fastest_traits: Sepals 18–30 mm, lanceolate to lance-ovate, usually hispid

look_alikes.distinction: Both can have large blue-purple flowers and hairy foliage. I. lindheimeri is perennial and combines a very large 55–90 mm corolla with 18–30 mm sepals and strongly lobed hairy leaves; confirm habit plus calyx rather than color.
I. cordatotriloba has much smaller flowers (20–38 mm) and shorter 8–14 mm sepals.
